questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: A turning stroke counted once
questions.learningObjective: Identify a turning stroke in a table entry

stimulus.body: A data table lists 九 with two strokes and notes that the second stroke turns without lifting the brush.

questions.stem: 请根据材料回答：In a field notebook, how many strokes does the table assign to the turning second stroke?

options.text: Two strokes, because it turns midway through.选项：
options.misconception: counts direction changes as new strokes

options.text: Zero strokes, because turns are not counted at all.选项：
options.misconception: treats "Zero strokes, because turns are not counted at all" as if it followed from the evidence

options.text: One stroke, because the turn happens without a lift.选项：
Three strokes, because the table counts every bend.选项：
options.misconception: mistakes a surface feature of "Three strokes, because the table counts every…" for the governing rule

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: the turn is part of one stroke because the brush stays down. On that basis "One stroke, because the turn happens without a lift" is the supported choice. questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: Adding the parts of a character
questions.learningObjective: Sum strokes for a two-part character

stimulus.body: 下面是一则简短材料，用来考查这一用法的理解。「Six strokes, by adding two and four directly.」 材料后给出四个选项，只有一个选项与材料本身所提供的信息相符。

questions.stem: 结合提示“Adding the parts of a character”，哪一项真正得到材料的支持？.

options.text: Four strokes, by counting only the tree part and ignoring the radical.
options.misconception: counts only the phonetic part and ignores radical

options.text: Seven strokes, by adding one joining stroke between parts.
options.misconception: adds a phantom joining stroke between parts

options.text: Two strokes, by counting only the radical and ignoring the rest.
options.misconception: counts only the radical and ignores the rest

options.text: Six strokes, by adding two and four directly.

questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: no extra joining stroke is added. On that basis "Six strokes, by adding two and four directly" is the supported choice. Option A ("Four strokes, by counting only the tree part and ignoring the…") fails because it counts only the phonetic part and ignores radical; Option B ("Seven strokes, by adding one joining stroke between parts") fails because it adds a phantom joining stroke between parts; Option C ("Two strokes, by counting only the radical and ignoring the rest") fails because it counts only the radical and ignores the rest.
